reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Definitions for child employment in entertainment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1)-(3)) and source notes (L. 1995 H.B. 300 & 95 merged with H.B. 414). Defines "employer," "entertainment industry" (motion picture, television, radio, theatrical, modeling, horse shows, rodeos, and musical performances), and "work permit" (for children under 16, generally 12 months and renewable at next birthday).

headings.title: Entertainment work permit requirement and documentation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 (including subdivisions (1)-(3)) and source notes (1995 merged enactments). Prohibits employing a child in the entertainment industry without a director-issued work permit requiring proof of age, written parental/custodian/guardian consent, and a prospective employer's filed written statement of employment nature and projected duration upon contractual agreement.

headings.title: Required presence of parent, guardian, or written designee
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (1995 merged enactments). Prohibits permitting a child at the place of employment without a parent, legal custodian, guardian, or designated guardian present at all times (with access to wardrobe, makeup, hairdressing, and dressing rooms), and allows written signed designation of an accompanying individual kept on file at the site.

headings.title: Designated on-site child welfare coordinator
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (1995 merged enactments). Requires the employer to designate one individual on each set, stage, or workplace to coordinate child welfare matters and notify each child's parent, legal custodian, or guardian of that coordinator's name.

headings.title: Required meal periods and maximum continuous hours
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (1995 merged enactments). Excludes meal periods from allowed workplace hours, requires meal periods of 30 to 60 minutes, and prohibits keeping a child at the workplace longer than five and one-half hours without a meal break.

headings.title: Twelve-hour between-workday and fifteen-minute rest breaks
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 and source notes (1995 merged enactments). Requires a 12-hour rest break between workdays for the same employment and a 15-minute rest period after each two hours of continuous work.

headings.title: Suitable on-site rest or play area
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 and source notes (1995 merged enactments). Requires the employer to provide a suitable place for children to rest or play at the site of employment.

headings.title: Counting rehearsals, practice, meal breaks, and rest breaks
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 8 and source notes (1995 merged enactments). Counts time spent in rehearsals and learning or practicing arts for or under direction of a motion picture studio, theater, or television studio—as well as rest breaks—as work time, while excluding meal breaks from overall work time.

headings.title: Prohibition on clear danger and child's right to refuse
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 9 and source notes (1995 merged enactments). Prohibits requiring a child to work in clear and present danger to life or limb, and bars requiring performance if the child believes such danger exists after discussing it with a parent/guardian/designee and employer, regardless of the belief's validity or reasonableness.

headings.title: Qualified trainer required for dangerous animals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 10 and source notes (1995 merged enactments). Prohibits requiring a child to work with an animal a reasonable person would regard as dangerous under the circumstances unless an animal trainer or handler qualified by training and experience is present.

headings.title: Stunt and hazardous-activity consent, medical aid, and first-aid kits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 11 and source notes (1995 merged enactments). Requires prior consultation before stunts, prior written parental/custodian/guardian consent plus available emergency medical personnel and emergency transport for unusual physical/athletic/acrobatic activities, stunts, special effects, or potentially hazardous activities, and always-available first-aid kits at the workplace.

headings.title: Prohibited proximity to explosives and dangerous moving parts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 12 and source notes (1995 merged enactments). Prohibits a child from working in close proximity to explosives, functioning parts of unguarded dangerous moving equipment, aircraft, or vessels, or functioning blades or propellers.

headings.title: No authorization for unlawful school absence
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 13 and source notes (1995 merged enactments). Clarifies that an entertainment work permit does not authorize school absence violating state law or regulations/policies of the state board of education, DESE, or local school board.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 13 subsections (including subdivisions (1)-(3) of subs 1 and 2) and source notes (L. 1995 H.B. 300 & 95 merged with H.B. 414) and verified all fingerprints. Checked entertainment definitions, director work permit documentation, parent/guardian/written-designee presence, child welfare coordinator, meal periods (30-60 min, max 5.5 hours without meal), 12-hour between-workday and 15-minute rest breaks, rest/play area, rehearsal/practice/break time counting, clear-danger prohibition and subjective child refusal right, qualified dangerous-animal trainer, stunt and hazardous-activity consultation/consent/emergency medical coverage/first-aid kits, explosive/moving-part proximity ban, and school-absence disclaimer. Revised sub 6 ('between-workday' rather than 'overnight') and sub 11 (covering hazardous activities beyond stunts); retained subs 1-5, 7-10, and 12-13.

headings.title: Daily, weekly, and normal hour limits and entertainment waivers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 9621 through A.L. 2002 S.B. 923, et al.; prior revisions 1929-1909; cross-reference to section 178.330 counting part-time school attendance as employment time). Limits child gainful employment to 3 hours per school day, 8 hours per nonschool day, 6 days/40 hours per week, and 7:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. (subject to subsection 2), with written director waivers permitted only for section 294.022 entertainment employment.

headings.title: Seasonal curfews, fair and school exceptions, and entertainment waivers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (including section 178.330 cross-reference). Sets evening cutoffs of 7:00 p.m. (Labor Day to June 1) and 9:00 p.m. (June 1 to Labor Day), creates a conditional regional-fair exception until 10:30 p.m. for ages 14-15 (excluding FLSA-covered entities), exempts children permanently excused from school under chapter 167, and permits written director waivers only for section 294.022 employment.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and all source notes (RSMo 1939 § 9621 through A.L. 2002 S.B. 923, et al.; prior revisions 1929-1909; cross-reference note to section 178.330 counting part-time school attendance as employment time) and verified all fingerprints. Verified daily/weekly/7 a.m.-9 p.m. normal-hour limits and section 294.022-only written director waivers in sub 1, and seasonal 7 p.m./9 p.m. evening curfews, conditional regional-fair exception until 10:30 p.m. for ages 14-15 excluding FLSA-covered entities, chapter 167 permanent school-excuse exclusion, and section 294.022-only written waivers in sub 2. Revised sub 1 title to include normal hour limits and sub 2 title to specify entertainment waivers.

headings.title: Authorized issuers of work certificates, oversight, and limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1)-(4) and paragraphs (4)(a)-(c)) and source notes (L. 1957 p. 525 § 7, A.L. 1986 H.B. 1554 Revision, A.L. 2010 H.B. 1892). Authorizes public school superintendents, charter school CEOs, authorized student-services certificate holders, and public/private school principals (or designees) to issue work certificates, subject to principal self-certification, copies to the district superintendent, superintendent revocation power, and a bar on issuing to one's own child with an exception for primary education providers of chapter 167 home-educated/privately tutored students. Note: official catchline names only the superintendent, whereas subsection 1 text covers additional issuers.

headings.title: Alternate issuer when designated certificated person is unavailable
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (1957-2010 amendments). Permits another person authorized by the school district superintendent or charter school CEO (or equivalent) to issue a work certificate if the designated certificated person is unavailable and delay would jeopardize the child's ability to secure work.

headings.title: Temporary issuer authorization during superintendent or CEO absence
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (1957-2010 amendments). If a district or charter school has no student-services certificate holder, permits written authorization of a non-credentialed person to issue work certificates during the superintendent's or charter CEO's absence.

headings.title: Hour limitations based on child's school calendar
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (1957-2010 amendments). Notwithstanding chapter 294 or other law, ties hour limitations for any subsection 1 work certificate to the school calendar of the school the child attends.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections (including sub 1 subdivisions (1)-(4) and paragraphs (4)(a)-(c)) and source notes (L. 1957 p. 525 § 7, A.L. 1986 H.B. 1554 Revision, A.L. 2010 H.B. 1892) and verified all fingerprints. Confirmed that sub 1 text is broader than the official catchline ('Superintendent of schools to issue work certificates'), authorizing public school superintendents, charter school CEOs, authorized student-services certificate holders, and public/private school principals (or designees) subject to self-certification, copies, revocation, and own-child limits with the chapter 167 home-education/private-tutor exception; also verified alternate/temporary issuers in subs 2-3 and school-calendar hour limits in sub 4. Retained all 4 drafted titles.

headings.title: Required information on work certificates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1)-(4)) and source notes (L. 1957 p. 525 § 8). Lists required contents of a work certificate: the child's age, sex, birthplace, birthdate, and residence; parent, guardian, or custodian's name and residence; employer's name and address; and nature of employment.

headings.title: Distinct form and color for nonschool-hours certificates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1957 p. 525 § 8). Requires work certificates authorizing nonschool-hours employment to be of a form and color distinct from full-time employment certificates.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections (including sub 1 subdivisions (1)-(4)) and source notes (L. 1957 p. 525 § 8) and verified all fingerprints. Verified required certificate contents in sub 1 and distinct form and color for nonschool-hours certificates in sub 2. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Transmitting and filing certificates or permits and posting minor list
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 9624 through A.L. 2002 S.B. 923, et al.; prior revisions 1929-1909). Directs issuing officers to transmit granted work certificates or permits to employers and copies to the division, and requires employers to keep them on file and conspicuously post a list of all employed children under age 16.

headings.title: Returning work certificate or permit upon termination
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (1939-2002). Requires employers to immediately return a child's work certificate or work permit to the issuing officer upon termination of the child's employment.

headings.title: Issuing new certificate or permit after return
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (1939-2002). Permits issuing a new work certificate or work permit for a child whose prior certificate or permit was returned by the employer to the issuing officer.

headings.title: Retaining and transmitting issued and cancelled copies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (1939-2002). Requires issuing officers to retain a copy of each issued work certificate or work permit and any cancellation notice and transmit a copy to the division.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 9624 through A.L. 2002 S.B. 923, et al.; prior revisions 1929-1909) and verified all fingerprints. Checked transmission/filing of work certificates or work permits and conspicuous posting of under-16 employees in sub 1, immediate return upon termination in sub 2, reissuance after return in sub 3, and retention/transmission of issued and cancellation copies in sub 4. Revised sub 1 title to include work permits alongside certificates; retained subs 2-4.

headings.title: Director enforcement, inspection, and document production powers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 9626 through A.L. 2002 S.B. 923, et al.; prior revision 1929 § 14091). Charges the director with enforcing chapter 294 and child-employment laws, granting supervision, workplace entry and inspection rights, and authority to require production of work certificates, permits, and specifically requested employment documents.

headings.title: Two-year employer recordkeeping of certificates and hours
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (1939-2002). Requires employers subject to sections 294.005 to 294.150 or related regulations to keep on-premises for at least two years each child's work certificate, name, address, age, and daily times and hours worked.

headings.title: Confidentiality of division records pertaining to minors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (1939-2002). Declares division records and information pertaining to minors confidential and prohibits disclosure of personal identifying information except by order of a court of competent jurisdiction.

headings.title: Cancellation of work certificate or permit and employment bar
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (1939-2002). Requires reporting improperly granted, illegally used, or injurious employment to the issuing officer for cancellation, immediate written notice with reasons to the child and employer, and makes continued employment unlawful thereafter.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 9626 through A.L. 2002 S.B. 923, et al.; prior revision 1929 § 14091) and verified all fingerprints. Verified director enforcement, inspection, and document-production powers in sub 1, two-year on-premises employer recordkeeping under sections 294.005 to 294.150 in sub 2, confidentiality of division records and court-order limit on personal identifying information in sub 3, and work certificate/permit cancellation and employment bar in sub 4. Retained all 4 drafted titles.

headings.title: Civil damages, separate violations, and enforcement suits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1995 H.B. 300 & 95 § 294.120 merged with H.B. 414 § 294.120, A.L. 2002 S.B. 923, et al.). Imposes civil damages of $50 to $1,000 per violation in addition to section 294.110 criminal liability, makes each continuing day and each child a separate violation, and authorizes enforcement suits by the director or the attorney general on the director's behalf.

headings.title: Factors for determining civil damages and maximum requests
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 (including subdivisions (1)-(8)) and source notes (1995-2002). Requires the director to base requested civil damages on violation nature/gravity and business employee count, and lists eight factors (individually or combined) justifying a request for maximum civil damages.

headings.title: Certified-mail violation notice and required contents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 (including subdivisions (1)-(6)) and source notes (1995-2002). Requires certified-mail notice when the director decides to seek civil damages, specifying violation nature and date, involved child(ren)'s names, requested damages, settlement terms, and right to contest.

headings.title: Finality of initial determination unless contested within twenty days
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (1995-2002). Makes the division's initial violation determination final unless the charged party notifies the director in writing within 20 calendar days after mailing that it is being contested.

headings.title: Contesting division determination and director review meeting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (1995-2002). Permits named parties to contest a violation determination by written appeal received by the director within 20 calendar days of mailing, requiring a director review meeting and either upholding or revising the determination.

headings.title: Appealing director determination to department director
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 and source notes (1995-2002). Allows written appeal of a subsequent violation determination to the department director within 20 calendar days of mailing (else the director's determination becomes final), requiring a review meeting by the department director or designee to uphold or revise. Source phrasing retained verbatim: sentence 3 refers to 'If the director does not receive the written appeal' after sentences 1-2 direct filing with the department director, and sentence 5 reads 'may hold that the findings of the division and the director to support the violation determination.'

headings.title: Finality of department determination and chapter 536 review
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 and source notes (1995-2002). Makes the determination of the department director or designee the final violation determination unless judicial review is sought under chapter 536.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 7 subsections (including subdivisions (1)-(8) of sub 2 and (1)-(6) of sub 3) and source notes (L. 1995 H.B. 300 & 95 § 294.120 merged with H.B. 414 § 294.120, A.L. 2002 S.B. 923, et al.) and verified all fingerprints. Checked civil damages/separate violations/director-or-AG suits in sub 1, damages/maximum-request factors in sub 2, certified-mail notice contents in sub 3, 20-day finality and director review meeting in subs 4-5, appeal to department director in sub 6 (retaining exact archived text where sentence 3 says 'If the director does not receive' and sentence 5 reads 'may hold that the findings of the division and the director to support the violation determination'), and department finality/chapter 536 judicial review in sub 7. Retained all 7 drafted titles and expanded sub 6 reviewNote.

headings.title: Creation, deposits, and enforcement use of fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1995 H.B. 300 & 95 § 294.130 merged with H.B. 414 § 294.130). Creates the "Child Labor Enforcement Fund" in the state treasury for court-awarded civil damages and chapter 294 settlement moneys, to be used subject to appropriation by the division of labor standards for chapter 294 investigations and enforcement.

headings.title: Biennial reversion threshold notwithstanding section 33.080
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (1995 merged enactments). Notwithstanding section 33.080, bars transfer to general revenue unless the biennial fund balance exceeds twice the preceding fiscal year's appropriations, lapsing only the excess.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and source notes (L. 1995 H.B. 300 & 95 § 294.130 merged with H.B. 414 § 294.130) and verified all fingerprints. Verified Child Labor Enforcement Fund creation, deposits of civil damages and settlements, and appropriation-conditioned division use in sub 1, and biennial 2x reversion threshold notwithstanding section 33.080 in sub 2. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Director rulemaking authority with department and commission approval
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1995 H.B. 300 & 95 merged with H.B. 414). Authorizes the director, subject to approval of the department director and the commission, to adopt, amend, or rescind rules necessary to administer chapter 294.

headings.title: Joint committee approval and delegation terms for rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (1995 merged enactments). States in archived statutory text that no rule promulgated under chapter 294 becomes effective without Joint Committee on Administrative Rules approval and makes legislative delegation dependent on JCAR review/suspension pending legislative ratification; describes archived text without certifying current enforceability.

headings.title: Concurrent submission of proposed rules and committee hearings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (1995 merged enactments). Describes archived statutory text requiring concurrent submission of proposed rules to the joint committee upon secretary-of-state filing and authorizing committee hearings at any time; neutral description without certifying current enforceability.

headings.title: Thirty-day review window before filing final rulemaking orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (1995 merged enactments). Describes archived statutory text barring filing of a final order of rulemaking with the secretary of state until 30 days after committee receipt, allowing hearings during that period, and deeming an order approved if not disapproved within 30 days; neutral description without certifying current enforceability.

headings.title: Grounds for joint committee suspension of rulemaking orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 (including subdivisions (1)-(4)) and source notes (1995 merged enactments). Describes archived statutory text authorizing majority-vote committee suspension of a rulemaking order prior to filing solely for lack of statutory authority, public health/safety/welfare emergency, conflict with state law, or substantial change in circumstance; neutral description without certifying current enforceability.

headings.title: Filing and publication bar for disapproved rule portions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 and source notes (1995 merged enactments). Describes archived statutory text prohibiting the director from filing committee-disapproved rule portions with the secretary of state and barring Missouri Register publication of disapproved portions; neutral description without certifying current enforceability.

headings.title: Legislative ratification of joint committee rule disapproval
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 and source notes (1995 merged enactments). Describes archived statutory text directing the committee to report disapproval findings to the senate and house and preventing a disapproved rule portion from taking effect if both houses ratify the disapproval by resolution within 30 legislative days; neutral description without certifying current enforceability.

headings.title: General assembly suspension or revocation of adopted rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 8 and source notes (1995 merged enactments). Describes archived statutory text providing for general assembly suspension or revocation of adopted rules by bill or Article IV, Section 8 concurrent resolution upon JCAR recommendation, with section 536.037 hearing authority and Missouri Register notice publication; neutral description without certifying current enforceability.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 8 subsections (including sub 5 subdivisions (1)-(4)) and source notes (L. 1995 H.B. 300 & 95 merged with H.B. 414) and verified all fingerprints. Verified director rulemaking subject to department director and commission approval in sub 1 and archived 1995 Joint Committee on Administrative Rules approval, concurrent submission, 30-day final-order window, four suspension grounds, filing/publication bar, legislative ratification, and general assembly suspension/revocation provisions in subs 2-8. Revised sub 2 title to neutral 'Joint committee approval and delegation terms for rules' and ensured subs 2-8 reviewNotes explicitly frame the headings as neutral descriptions of archived statutory text without certifying current enforceability; retained subs 1 and 3-8 titles.
